newsitem.title: USA: Treasury's Rubin not worried about EMU prospects.
newsitem.headline: Treasury's Rubin not worried about EMU prospects.

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin on Thursday said he was not worried by concerns about the prospects for developing a single European currency in 1999.

"I have not heard anybody express major concerns," Rubin said in response to a reporter's question about whether elections in Europe could spell trouble for European monetary union. "I really have no great worries about it," he said.
Rubin said EMU may be discussed by monetary officials in Washington for International Monetary Fund and Group of Seven meetings, but he said he did not know how much time would be devoted to it.
Rubin also said it was up to Japanese policymakers to achieve domestic demand-led growth while avoiding a significant increase in its current account surplus.
"How they (Japan) do that is obviously the business of their policymakers," Rubin told reporters when asked whether he was prepared to take action if the surplus rose.
Rubin also told reporters he would be meeting with his counterparts from Germany and Japan over the weekend ahead of the Group of Seven gathering on Sunday.
